players.product: sputtering targets and electronic materials for semiconductor manufacturing

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 RESULTS (first full standalone quarter): CEO David Sewell said net sales of $991 million were up 10% year-over-year and 'exceeded the top end of our guidance'; adjusted EBITDA was $249 million, relatively flat year-over-year, at a 25.1% margin. CFO Tina Pierce said organic growth was 8% (6% volume, 2% pricing), with volume growth in nuclear, refrigerants and electronic materials.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $991 million, up 10%; adjusted EBITDA $249 million; margin 25.1%

quarterly_data.signal: ELECTRONIC MATERIALS ACCELERATING ON SEMICONDUCTOR DEMAND: electronic materials delivered '21% year-on-year revenue growth following 19% year-on-year growth in the fourth quarter of 2025'. CFO: electronic materials net sales rose 21% to $109 million, 'driven by volume growth and robust customer demand across semiconductor applications'; the Electronic & Specialty Materials segment posted $281 million net sales (+7%) and $58 million adjusted EBITDA (20.8% margin). Management ties the growth to 'the ongoing shift to advanced nodes and advanced packaging' and to 'secular trends for AI and data centers'.
quarterly_data.figure: electronic materials increased 21% to $109 million (after 19% growth in Q4 2025); ESM segment $281 million, 7% growth

quarterly_data.signal: SPOKANE SPUTTERING-TARGET CAPACITY DOUBLING: Solstice is 'investing $200 million in our Spokane, Washington facility to double our target's capacity, reduce customer lead times'. CEO calls its sputtering targets 'the materials of choice for leading-edge semiconductor nodes used for AI and data center applications' and expects the project to exceed its 'mid-teens percentage IRR' hurdle; it is 'evaluating opportunities to further accelerate similar organic growth investments'.
quarterly_data.figure: $200 million to double sputtering-target capacity at Spokane

quarterly_data.signal: SOLD OUT AT SPOKANE, EXPANSION BEING PULLED IN: asked whether electronics would become capacity constrained before the expansion starts up, the CEO said 'we're, for lack of a better word, selling everything we can make in our Spokane facility' and are working 'to accelerate the expansion that we're doing, looking at it in a little bit of a modular design'. He said its 'technology in copper manganese is a better technical solution' getting 'broader adoption in the marketplace', expects leading-edge-node growth to continue 'going into the 2030s', and said the TIMs (thermal interface) business is also seeing significant growth and working on expansion. Separately, the CEO said growth capex projects that were originally multi-year (full benefit '2-3 years out') are being pulled in for electronics and defense 'because the demand is so strong', giving returns earlier.

GUIDANCE AND CAPEX: full-year 2026 guidance reaffirmed (net sales between $3.9 billion and $4.1 billion; adjusted EBITDA between $975 million and $1.025 billion; capex between $400 million to $425 million). First-time Q2 2026 guide: net sales between $1.06 billion and $1.1 billion at an approximately 25%-26% adjusted EBITDA margin, assuming continued momentum in refrigerants, nuclear and electronic materials; includes $10 million of planned downtime-related expense. Q1 capex was $82 million, a 32% increase year-over-year, for growth projects including the Spokane electronic-materials expansion.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales $3.9 billion to $4.1 billion (reaffirmed); Q2 net sales $1.06 billion to $1.1 billion; Q1 capex $82 million, a 32% increase

players.product: low-GWP refrigerants and thermal-management fluids for data-center cooling

quarterly_data.signal: REFRIGERANTS +19% WITH ACCELERATING DATA-CENTER ORDERS: CFO said refrigerants net sales increased 19% year-over-year to $389 million on favorable pricing and volume, and 'benefited from accelerating orders for data centers'. The Refrigerants & Applied Solutions segment had $711 million net sales (+12%) and $242 million adjusted EBITDA at a 34.1% margin, down 522 basis points on refrigerant mix (HFO transition) and higher R&D. CEO: 'The 19% growth was mostly driven through HFOs'.
quarterly_data.figure: refrigerants increased 19% to $389 million; RAS segment $711 million, 12% growth; margin 34.1%

quarterly_data.signal: DATA-CENTER REFRIGERANTS GROWING DOUBLE DIGITS; TWO-PHASE DIRECT-TO-CHIP NEXT: CEO said 'we are definitely seeing double-digit growth in refrigerants in data centers' (not quantified; Solstice is 'a step removed' but has 'line of sight' via customers). It has 'multiple projects co-innovating with customers, both on the chip side and at the data center infrastructure side': 'single-phase direct to chip, which is kind of happening now. I think you'll see soon two-phase direct to chip', with immersion cooling explored over 'the next four or five years'. Also working with data centers on reusing waste heat; this co-innovation is driving higher R&D spend.

HFO MIX SHIFT AND MARGIN TURN: CEO said Solstice entered 2026 at 'about a ratio of 60% HFOs, 40% HFCs' and expects to 'approach 70/30' exiting 2026 into 2027. 'Now, approximately four quarters into the R-454B transition', management expects sequential refrigerant margin improvement from Q1 levels, and wants to 'establish ourselves as a strong leader' in data centers with HFOs.
